apps.subtitle: PlayStation 2 games on iPhone and iPad. Needs JIT.
apps.localizedDescription:
Play your PS2 games on iPhone and iPad.
You need your own PS2 BIOS and game files, and JIT for full speed. None of it is included.

ARMSX2 is a native ARM64 build of PCSX2. The recompilers run on your device instead of translating x86 code, which is what makes PS2 emulation workable on a phone. They are the shared ARM64 recompilers, checked by comparing what they execute against other emulators, and they apply the game database's own patches as a game runs.

What you get
- On-screen controls you can move and resize, with separate portrait and landscape layouts
- Controller skins, browsed and installed inside the app with a preview and the author on every row, or brought in yourself as .armsx2skin, Delta or ManicEMU. Each game can keep its own
- Per-game settings, so a fix for one game does not follow you into the next
- RetroAchievements, with your account, your progress and the achievement list in the app, and unlocks arriving as ordinary iOS notifications. Hardcore Mode still allows trusted widescreen and 60 FPS patches, and still blocks cheats
- Save states and virtual memory cards
- Save states from AetherSX2 and NetherSX2 builds load directly, once you copy them in through Files
- A frame rate cap that limits presentation only, to cut heat and battery drain
- An on-screen performance overlay
- External controllers, plus adjustable phone haptics
- Live backgrounds behind the menus: twelve built in, including a PS2 menu and an XMB recreation, or your own image or video, set separately for portrait and landscape
- Ten alternate app icons

Requirements
iPhone or iPad on iOS 17 or later. JIT is what gets you full speed. Without it ARMSX2 falls back to an interpreter rather than refusing to start, flags it with a No JIT badge while you play, and most games are too slow to enjoy. Disc images open straight from Files: .iso, .bin, .img, .chd and .rom.

How well a game runs depends on your device, your iOS version and the game itself. Some are perfect, some are slow, some do not boot. Check the compatibility list before you start.

Links

Compatibility: https://armsx2.net/compatibility
Docs and FAQ: https://armsx2.net/docs
Discord: https://discord.gg/S7VxwfS8w9
Source code: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2

Support development
Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/cw/ARMSX2
Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/armsx2

Credits:
ARMSX2 is open source under GPL-3.0 and builds on PCSX2. Started by MoonPower with support from jpolo1224, forked from PCSX2_ARM64 by Pontos.

App icon by fffathur, logo by Vivimagic. The icon artwork is MIT licensed: https://github.com/ARMSX2/Save-Tower

ARMSX2 does not include games or BIOS files. Donations are voluntary and the project seeks no commercial return. It is not officially associated with PCSX2 or with any other fork of it, and not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or PlayStation.

versions.localizedDescription:
Frame rate cap

@Henyckma added an FPS cap that limits presentation only. The game and the audio keep running at full speed, so it costs nothing in emulation and gives back battery and heat instead. Targets are 15, 23.976, 29.94, 30, 45, 59.97, 60, 90 and 120, set globally or per game. The gain is biggest at 2x and 3x internal resolution, where the passes it skips cover the most pixels. Selecting 30 FPS used to halve emulation and audio speed, which is fixed, and FPS profiles from earlier builds carry over without losing the cadence you picked.

Crashes and freezes

Fixed a crash in games like Namco Museum 50th Anniversary, which turned out to be an out of bounds write in the virtual memory page protection table. Fixed a freeze in readback heavy scenes with Hardware Download Mode set to Unsynchronized. Rogue Galaxy no longer stalls the graphics thread around 7.5 ms every frame on a depth probe readback, about a fifth of the frame on an M2. The last two are bmdhacks. Saving per game settings could also leave the game frozen a second or two later, which is covered below.

Sprite hacks

Align Sprite and Merge Sprite apply when you switch them off. This was the third report of that bug and the fifth attempt at it, and the earlier ones all fixed the global screen while leaving everything around it alone. Per game, those rows greyed out whenever GameDB Graphics Fixes was on, kept showing their old value, and got written back on every save. Align Sprite, Merge Sprite and Wild Arms Offset are one Use Global / Off / On picker each now, and they no longer need manual hacks mode. Setting one claims that fix, so the game database stops overriding it while keeping every other fix for the game. Texture Inside RT, Native Scaling, Bilinear Upscale, Unscaled Palette Draw, Preload Frame Data and Disable Partial Invalidation had the same bug and were fixed with it. None of these do anything at 1x internal resolution, which is by design.

Per-game settings

Turning on Use Per-Game Overrides used to soften text and edges: enabling it copied six graphics keys into the per game file, and one of those forced a blend deinterlace that also suppressed the game's own database fix. Only the settings you change are written now. Saving in that panel could also leave the game frozen a second or two later while the emulator carried on at full speed, because metadata scans share one disc image with the running game and a scan during play left it holding a closed disc. 

The Renderer picker never saved a change made while a game was running, so it never applied either. It saves now, and it moved from Fixes & Compatibility to the Graphics tab where people kept looking for it. It still applies at the next boot of that game. Saving the panel is quicker too: it used to fire one full settings reload per field written, 71 of them for a single Save.

Settings

Every slider, stepper and typed number is one control now, and each setting is described once instead of once per screen. The FPS target had three different sets of bounds across three screens. Sliders stop on values people actually pick, every stop list holds the default so reset lands on one, and typing still reaches anything in between. Per game numbers can inherit the global value instead of choosing from a short list. The dynamic background sliders stay continuous, since every value there is a legitimate one, but they snap to the precision they print: a row could read 50% while storing 0.4973, which also left the reset arrow comparing against the hidden value.

Applying the Default preset asks first and then resets every setting, with the Default row showing as active afterwards, and Reset Graphics and Reset Emulator no longer reach into settings they do not show or drag Frame Pacing to Custom on the way. Buffer Size and Output Latency are sliders on Frame Pacing now, matching the Audio screen, and GS Back Thread says it needs a restart instead of looking broken. The preset fixes are @Henyckma's.

Rumble

Phone Rumble Strength runs on a scale that means something: off at 0%, the previous strength at 25%, and roughly three times that at 100%, with a separate Increase Duration of Rumble and Interpolation toggle that stretches how long an effect is felt without changing how strong it is. That changes what the stored value means, so existing settings are rescaled once on first launch rather than getting louder on update. Controller rumble is unchanged. Also @Henyckma.

Interface

The interface is dark everywhere now, whatever the device is set to. The library, the BIOS list and the settings screens used to follow the system while gameplay and the pause menu were already dark. There is a new App Icon screen under Interface with ten alternate icons.

Hide Menu Button stays hidden until you bring it back, and the choice survives restarting the app. Any controller press used to restore the button and switch the setting off with it. Tapping the game area shows it for about four seconds instead.

Booting without JIT shows a two stage warning now, and a red No JIT badge sits beside the Pause control while you play. Stop is on the Quick Menu and leaves the game straight away. The keyboard no longer flips the per game panel to the wrong layout, rotating no longer throws away unsaved edits, and Change Disc and Controller Skin line up with the rest of the pause menu. The no JIT warning and Quick Menu Stop are @Henyckma's.

Emulation accuracy

@bmdhacks and @pstef landed 26 EE and vector unit correctness fixes covering square root, min and max, the arctangent series, the multiplier's rounding and several flag paths. 23 of them cite hardware or console behaviour. 

Save states

Save states written by AetherSX2 v1.5-era builds and NetherSX2 v2.1 load directly, and saving over one writes a current format state. Voice, streaming and DMA state come back with them, so audio carries on instead of resetting. Pad, USB and achievement blocks in those older states predate the format ARMSX2 reads today and get skipped, so controllers keep whatever type and mode they booted with. There is no import button yet. Copy the file into the sstates folder in the ARMSX2 documents directory using the Files app, named the way ARMSX2 names its own: SERIAL (CRC).01.p2s

Thanks

Thanks to @bmdhacks for the save state loading, the accuracy work, the GS fixes and the Rogue Galaxy tuning, to @henyckma for the frame rate cap, the haptics, Quick Menu Stop, the preset resets and the no JIT warning, and to pstef for the EE multiplier work. Thanks as well to the testers who tracked down the per game text softening, the Namco Museum crash, and three separate rounds of Align Sprite.

Full commit list: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/iOSv2.5.1...iOSv2.5.2

2.5.1 is mostly a fixes release.

The two biggest issues were A12 devices crashing on launch and rumble being completely broken since 2.4.1. Both are fixed, along with a proper no-JIT fallback, several performance improvements, and a collection of Virtual Pad and interface fixes.

Highlights

 Fixed launch crashes on A12 devices
 Controller and phone rumble work again
 Added improved phone rumble with separate motor handling and a strength setting — @Henyckma
 Added a proper no-JIT fallback and improved interpreter performance — @Henyckma
 Fixed a Devil May Cry crash during FMVs
 Added fractional Internal Resolution options up to 3.5x
 Reduced graphics overhead in several games — @bmdhacks
 Improved Rogue Galaxy performance — @bmdhacks
 Virtual Pad and layout improvements — @Henyckma
 GameDB and cheat-loading fixes — @jpolo1224

A12 Devices

Fixed launch crashes on iPhone XS, XS Max, XR, iPad Air 3, iPad mini 5, iPad 8 and A12X/A12Z iPad Pro.

2.5.0 was accidentally built with an Apple M1 CPU baseline. iOS now targets apple-a12, the oldest device we support.

Rumble

Controller and phone rumble work again after being broken since 2.4.1.

@Henyckma also reworked phone rumble. It is now sustained, responds properly to motor strength, handles the two PS2 motors separately, and ramps in and out more naturally.

A Phone Rumble Strength setting has been added, and Test Rumble now works without a controller connected.

Several controller-rumble bugs were fixed at the same time, including a leak, a threading issue and cases where rumble could be routed to the wrong player.

Playing Without JIT

@Henyckma added a proper fallback for devices where JIT is unavailable.

Instead of crashing or showing a black screen, ARMSX2 now falls back to interpreter implementations where possible.

Interpreter performance was improved at the same time. On the test device and workload, EE time went from 37.55 ms to 30.55 ms, about 18.6% less. Results vary by game, device and thermal state.

Crashes and Stability

Fixed a Devil May Cry crash when the game switches to the software renderer for FMVs.

Several related JIT and software-renderer stability issues were fixed as well, including problems affecting legacy JIT mode under LiveContainer.

Fastmem now stays disabled correctly when its required 4 GB virtual mapping cannot be allocated, and a race in the JIT keepalive path was narrowed.

Graphics and Performance

@bmdhacks reduced unnecessary render-pass and copy work.

Across a five-loop replay:

 Rogue Galaxy: 2,411 → 1,741 render passes
 OutRun 2006: 1,240 → 1,118 render passes

Vertex processing was also reduced in cases where an auto-flush cannot occur. Dragon Quest VIII measured 4.7% fewer graphics-thread cycles in testing.

Internal Resolution now includes:

1.25x, 1.5x, 1.75x, 2.25x, 2.5x, 2.75x and 3.5x

Game Database

@bmdhacks improved Rogue Galaxy performance by disabling auto-flush for the game.

Render passes fall 38% and texture copies 74%, worth about 1.8 ms per frame and 2.6 fps on a low-end device.

There is a small visual trade-off: some lamp lighting can appear slightly brighter and warmer than the software renderer reference. Four side-by-side comparisons at 1:1 failed to distinguish the two, but please report it if you notice it during normal play.

Need for Speed Underground 1 and 2 now run without hardware readbacks — @jpolo1224.

Cheats stored under the generic all-CRC file name work again — @jpolo1224.

Virtual Pad

All of this is @Henyckma's.

Dynamic Thumbstick feedback now pulses once when crossing the maximum-pull threshold instead of repeating continuously.

Swipe Camera gets the same feedback once it becomes a joystick, and now uses the full left half of the screen on iPad.

Saved layouts now have Rename, Share and Delete options.

Device Presets no longer change Aspect Ratio or treat it as part of whether a preset is active.

Interface Fixes

 Fixed a crash when toggling Low Power Mode with a video wallpaper visible
 Fixed saved Dynamic Background colours sometimes loading as black
 Fixed incorrect Cancel behaviour in the colour editor
 Fixed the dark gradient slider not correctly showing why the effect was disabled
 Removed the unused Widen theme in portrait setting
 Fixed the skins search field being hidden under the tab bar on iOS 26
 Fixed the performance overlay showing PCSX2 instead of ARMSX2 2.5.1

Thanks

@Henyckma contributed the no-JIT fallback and interpreter work, rumble improvements, Virtual Pad changes and Device Presets fix.

@bmdhacks contributed the graphics optimizations and Rogue Galaxy tuning.

@jpolo1224 contributed the GameDB and cheat-loading fixes.

Thanks as well to everyone who tested the rumble changes and reported what still felt wrong between revisions.

ARMSX2 2.5.0 is a major update to the emulator core and the iOS frontend.

The biggest core change is a new shared ARM64 recompiler, replacing the older iOS-specific EE, IOP and VU recompilers. It brings iOS in line with the ARM handheld builds, reduces CPU overhead in several parts of emulation, and restores features the previous iOS backend did not support correctly.

The release also moves iOS onto the shared game database used by the other mobile ARM builds. That brings a large set of newer per-game fixes and tuning to iOS. Outside the core, 2.5.0 adds Dynamic Controls, animated backgrounds, settings presets, improved frame pacing, proper 120 Hz support, an in-app controller-skin browser, RetroAchievements fixes, OSD improvements, and a long list of graphics and stability fixes.

Almost none of this is my own work. The core belongs to @bmdhacks, the new iOS interface and control features to @Henyckma, and the rest to @pstef, @jpolo1224, @XDarkFallenX and Mart. Thanks to all of them, and to everyone who tested development builds and reported problems.

Highlights

 New shared ARM64 recompiler for the EE, IOP and vector units, from @bmdhacks
 Updated shared game database with newer fixes and tuning for more than a thousand games
 Dynamic Thumbsticks, Swipe Camera, Gyroscope Camera and Dynamic Actions, from @Henyckma
 Twelve Metal-rendered Dynamic Background styles, from @Henyckma
 Six settings presets plus import and export, from @Henyckma
 Emulation-Only Mode, which frees the device to the emulator once a game is running, from @Henyckma
 Reworked frame-pacing controls and per-game presets
 Proper 120 Hz support on ProMotion devices
 Apple GPU fixes for speckled graphics in games such as Black and God of War II, from @bmdhacks
 Fixes for upscaling hacks and settings that previously appeared not to apply
 In-app controller-skin browser and more reliable skin importing
 Working RetroAchievements statistics, achievement lists and native notifications
 OSD safe-area, rotation and performance-overlay fixes
 Several iOS crashes and core correctness bugs fixed

New ARM64 Recompiler

ARMSX2 now uses the newer shared ARM64 recompiler family written by @bmdhacks and tested primarily on ARM handheld hardware, replacing the older iOS-specific implementations.

The new backend has had considerably more testing, including differential tests that compare recompiled EE, IOP and VU execution against other emulator implementations. It also contains substantial optimization work around register handling, larger compiled blocks, vector instructions, calls and returns, unaligned memory accesses, and self-modifying code.

Several features that were missing from the previous iOS backend are also supported now:

 Dynamic game patches can be applied from the game database. Entries such as the ones used by Armored Core: Nine Breaker and Ratchet & Clank 2 previously had no effect on iOS.
 Goemon's TLB handling now has the required preload and invalidation hooks. The fix remains behind the existing game fix and would still benefit from a complete playthrough test.
 Delay-slot swapping is supported where the PS2 allows it.

The JIT has also been adapted to the different executable-memory paths used by the app, including the iOS 26 TXM paths, Simulator support, and the legacy path used on iOS 18 and earlier. 

Game Compatibility

iOS no longer ships its own separate merged game database. ARMSX2 now uses the shared database. The move onto the shared resources was done by @bmdhacks.

The previous iOS copy had fallen behind upstream. With the shared database, more than a thousand games have different behavioral entries compared with 2.4.1, and future mobile fixes no longer need to be copied separately into the iOS version.

Some of the more visible changes include:

 Hardware-readback tuning is now actually applied from the game database, thanks to @jpolo1224 making the database key work at all. Forty-eight games currently use it, including Black, Jak 3, God Hand, Driv3r, Downhill Domination, Rumble Racing and Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks.
 Ratchet: Deadlocked, Chaos Legion and True Crime: New York City now receive their intended VU0 synchronization settings on iOS.
 NFL 2K5 no longer hangs at the boot logo because of a timer/recompiler timing issue, fixed by @bmdhacks.
 Crazy Frog Racer picks up its deinterlacing, half-pixel-offset and native-scaling fixes.
 The Gift receives its sound-RPC synchronization patch.
 Magna Carta: Tears of Blood, Genji demo builds and other titles receive newer graphics and clamp-mode corrections.

Thanks to @XDarkFallenX for a number of the game-database corrections included here.

Dynamic Controls

This whole system is @Henyckma's work.

The virtual pad can still use fixed sticks, but 2.5.0 adds a new Dynamic Controls system for games that work better with touch input spread across the screen.

With Dynamic Thumbsticks, a stick appears where your thumb touches rather than remaining in one fixed position. Dead zone, maximum radius, feel, base opacity, stick opacity, trail opacity and optional activation haptics can all be configured.

There are also two new camera-control methods:

 Swipe Camera maps dragging on unused screen space to right-stick movement.
 Gyroscope Camera uses device motion for camera input, with sensitivity, dead zone, smoothing, acceleration, maximum rate and axis inversion settings.

Dynamic Actions can map actions directly to the thumbsticks. A stick press can Aim, a tap can Fire, and a quick tap can start Hold Fire. Face buttons can also be assigned to either stick.

Movement and look sensitivity can be adjusted separately for normal play and aiming. The aiming crosshair also has its own type, size, opacity and animation settings.

Two presets are included: Default and an MGS 3 preset.

Automatic fire is disabled while RetroAchievements Hardcore Mode is active. If Hardcore becomes active while automatic fire is running, it stops immediately.

Dynamic Backgrounds and UI

The animated backgrounds, the retained-tab navigation, the Liquid Glass work and the new game-launch transition are all @Henyckma's.

The Games, BIOS, Help and Settings interfaces can use live Metal-rendered backgrounds.

Twelve styles are included, covering ambient effects, particles, ribbons, PlayStation-inspired themes and face-button patterns. They include PlayStation 2 Menu by Henyckma and PlayStation 3 XMB by Mart. Mart's XMB recreation is included under the MIT licence and credited in the app.

Backgrounds stay active as you move between menu sections, so animations do not restart on every tab change. Video backgrounds can also keep their playback position and audio while navigating the menus.

Selecting a still image or video automatically disables Dynamic Background so the two background systems do not overlap. Background visibility can also be controlled for the individual menu sections.

The main tabs are now retained instead of being rebuilt when you switch between them. Scroll positions are preserved, transitions are smoother, and left/right swipes can be used to move between tabs. Library scrolling is also lighter, because the cards no longer publish their geometry back into the interface as you scroll.

Help has moved into Settings > About.

On iOS 17 and 18, the navigation bar has been updated with a compact translucent design. iOS 26 continues to use the system tab bar, and a Clear Liquid Glass UI option has been added under Appearance.

Game launching also has a new transition from the selected library card into the Metal game view. The VM starts immediately underneath the animation, and the transition can be disabled in Appearance.

Returning from a game leaves it paused behind a Now Running card with Resume and Stop controls. Shutdown also shows a visible Stopping… state instead of appearing unresponsive.

Boot errors are clearer as well. Trying to start a game or Boot BIOS without a usable BIOS now explains the problem, and launching without JIT access shows a dedicated warning with information about the configured JIT script.

Presets and Emulation-Only Mode

Both features come from @Henyckma.

A new Settings Presets screen provides six built-in profiles:

 Default
 Ultra Quality
 High Quality
 High Quality 30 FPS
 Performance
 Ultra Performance

Each preset shows which settings it changes. Device presets can provide an appropriate starting point, and configurations can be exported to a text file and imported again for sharing or moving between installs.

Emulation-Only Mode can release most of the frontend and optional services after a game has finished starting, leaving more of the device to the emulator.

Individual features can still be kept when needed, including patches, RetroAchievements, the OSD, Quick Menu and other optional services. Virtual controls are kept automatically when no external controller is connected.

The teardown process has also been made more reliable, including BIOS-only sessions.

Performance and Frame Pacing

Frame-pacing settings have been reorganized into one panel instead of being spread across several screens and configuration keys.

Five presets are available:

 Optimal
 Smooth
 Low Latency
 Battery Saver
 Custom

They cover the frame limiter, FPS target, vsync queue depth, host-refresh synchronization and audio buffering.

Per-game settings use the same controls and allow individual values to fall back to Use Global. Applying a named preset per game also carries its FPS target with it.

Existing customized setups are preserved during migration rather than being replaced with a preset.

ARMSX2 also properly unlocks 120 Hz displays now, so ProMotion devices are no longer limited to 60 Hz by the app's own display configuration.

Several shared ARM performance paths have also been improved. GS vertex processing, MTVU synchronization and 16-bit graphics readbacks come from @bmdhacks; the FMV color conversion from @pstef; the compressed-disc caching from @jpolo1224.

Again, most measurements for this work were taken on ARM handheld hardware rather than iPhones. A few examples from that testing:

 On an SM6115 handheld, an MTVU synchronization change took Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2 from 23.9 to 34.2 FPS in the tested workload.
 The updated NEON FMV color-conversion path took about 70% of the time of the previous version on Cortex-X1C and A78C cores.
 On an SD865 limited to 800 MHz, a native-resolution readback change reduced a 600-frame OutRun 2006 test from 16.2 ms to 15.4 ms per frame and also reduced run-to-run variation.

Compressed CHD images also have a larger decompressed-chunk cache, which helps games with seek patterns that repeatedly revisit recently read data.

Graphics Fixes

Several long-standing graphics problems have been fixed.

Apple GPU speckles

Small bright speckles could appear along triangle edges on Apple GPUs in games including Black and God of War II.

The problem came from differences between shader-written depth values and the values used by later fixed-function depth testing. The affected path is now avoided on Apple GPUs.

Against the software renderer, the problematic pixels in one God of War II Athena-statue test dropped from 220 to 1. A Black test dropped from 762 differing pixels to 2. Diagnosed and fixed by @bmdhacks.

Dirge of Cerberus render passes

A new render-pass scheduler, also from @bmdhacks, can combine compatible hardware draws instead of opening a separate Metal pass for each one.

This is currently enabled only where the game database requests it. In a four-frame Dirge of Cerberus capture, the number of render passes fell from 8,035 to roughly 500.

Games that do not have this render-target pattern do not use the option.

Texture-pool slowdown

A texture-pool aging bug could cause some scenes to become slow until a settings screen was opened. Texture aging now happens on every frame, including when duplicate frames are skipped. Found and fixed by @jpolo1224.

iOS 17 startup crash

GPU enumeration used a Metal API that is only available on iOS 18 or later. On iOS 17 this could crash during graphics-device startup. The affected calls are now correctly version-gated.

Replacement textures

If a replacement texture fails to upload, ARMSX2 now drops it and uses the game's original texture instead of continuing with invalid texture contents. This addresses cases such as missing cursors or partially drawn text in large replacement packs, and comes from @jpolo1224.

Upscaling and Hardware-Fix Settings

Several problems made options such as Align Sprite appear to be stuck or ignored. These have been addressed together.

Graphics settings that can be applied while a game is running now reach the renderer correctly. The Renderer setting remains restart-only because changing it requires rebuilding the graphics device.

Changing a geometry-related hack also clears cached render targets where the previous adjustment may already have been baked into the image. This prevents old shifted geometry from remaining visible after a setting is disabled.

Game-database fixes can now be overridden per hack instead of requiring Manual Hardware Fixes to be enabled for everything. If you manually claim a setting such as Align Sprite, that choice overrides the database for that one option while the rest of the game's automatic fixes remain active.

The settings screen can also show the effective value currently used by the emulator and explain why it differs from the value you selected, such as a game-database override, automatic fix, per-game setting or 1x internal-resolution restriction.

One behavior has intentionally changed: manual hardware fixes are no longer applied to the BIOS screen or boot logo.

Controller Skins and ARMSX2 Folder

Community controller skins can now be installed directly from Browse Skins in Virtual Pad settings.

The browser includes previews, author information, download sizes, search and refresh support. Download and installation errors are also reported more clearly. The catalogue itself is maintained by bagasromadon, and the skins in it by their individual authors.

Manual importing has been made more tolerant:

 Some malformed manifests containing stray control characters can now be repaired and read.
 Layouts that exist in a package but were omitted from its manifest can be detected automatically when the match is unambiguous.
 Re-importing an installed skin offers Replace, Keep Both or Cancel instead of silently creating a duplicate.
 Replacement imports preserve per-game skin and layout selections.
 Archives created on macOS no longer fail because of MACOSX folders or . sidecar files.

You can also select an ARMSX2 Folder containing BIOS files, games, presets and skins. Access is remembered so the folder can be rescanned later, and newer versions of installed skin archives can be imported when the file on disk changes. The folder importer is @Henyckma's.

RetroAchievements

The RetroAchievements panel now displays actual account and game information.

User statistics, current-game progress and the achievement list were previously connected to unimplemented core functions, leaving the panel empty. Those functions are implemented in 2.5.0.

Achievement notifications have also been moved to the native iOS toast system instead of going through an unused fullscreen overlay. Unlocks, mastery, leaderboard events, login messages and connection changes now appear through the native interface with the configured display duration.

A crash involving the lifetime of pending toast data has also been fixed. Thanks to @Henyckma for finding and fixing that one, and for the Hardcore automatic-fire restrictions described above.

On-Screen Display

The OSD now respects the real UIKit safe area in each orientation.

Previously, the calculated safe-area information never reached the overlay, which could place top-right content too close to rounded corners or the Dynamic Island. Safe-area handling now works for the performance block and message toasts.

The performance overlay also shrinks when necessary so long lines remain on-screen after rotating to a narrower orientation.

Battery, thermal and memory information has returned to the overlay after being lost during the move to the shared core.

Rotating the device while the pause menu or per-game settings are open also updates those panels to the new orientation correctly.

Stability and Correctness

2.5.0 contains a number of fixes that do not fit neatly into the sections above:

 A late signal during fallback from the iOS TXM JIT path can no longer kill the app during startup.
 An out-of-bounds read in the sprite-merge path has been fixed by @jpolo1224.
 A low-level iOS symbol collision affecting bundle-path and Metal-layer helpers has been corrected.
 PS2 shift amounts are now masked to the width used by the real hardware, fixing inconsistent behavior between the interpreter and recompilers and removing a possible out-of-bounds host read. Verified by @pstef against a probe run on a real console.
 The IOP interpreter now handles jalr correctly when the target and link registers are the same. Also @pstef.
 Per-game stick inversion settings opened from the library now load and save correctly even when no VM is running.
 Reset All Overrides now includes virtual-pad layout, controller skin and inversion settings.
 The Cheats and Patches screen now distinguishes between Hardcore Mode being selected and Hardcore actually being active, instead of claiming features are already blocked before a game has booted.

Thanks

A large part of the core work in 2.5.0 came from the shared ARM development effort rather than from iOS-only changes, and most of what is new in the iOS app itself was written by @Henyckma.

@bmdhacks wrote the new recompiler family, the Apple GPU depth fixes, the render-pass scheduler, the GS vertex and MTVU work, and the move onto the shared game database.

@Henyckma wrote Dynamic Controls, the Dynamic Background system, Settings Presets, Emulation-Only Mode, the ARMSX2 Folder importer, the retained-tab and Liquid Glass navigation, the game-launch transition, and the RetroAchievements toast fix.

@pstef contributed the FMV color-conversion rewrite and two correctness fixes verified against real PS2 hardware. @jpolo1224 contributed the texture-pool, hardware-readback, sprite-merge, replacement-texture and CHD caching fixes. @XDarkFallenX contributed game-database corrections, and Mart's XMB recreation ships under the MIT licence.

And thanks to the testers who kept reporting the small things that were easy to dismiss as configuration problems. Several fixes in this release started with somebody demonstrating that a setting, game or screen really was behaving differently from what the emulator claimed.

ARMSX2 2.6.2 

Emulation Fixes: 

ESPN NFL 2K5 no longer freezes during early gameplay and now works as intended. 

Ratchet & Clank: Deadlocked, restored two COP2/VU0 sync fixes lost in the monorepo migration, plus a monotonic-clock guard that stopped the EE being slammed backwards. Game is now playable, although one graphical issue remains from my testing.

Folder memory cards work on a custom data folder again. Creating save data crashed or reported "format failed" for anyone whose data folder wasn't internal app storage. 

Texture Packs:

Importing a pack no longer freezes the app when using an SD card. A real pack is thousands of files over SAF, and the copy ran on the UI thread,  black screen, then "ARMSX2 isn't responding", worse on SD. ARMSX2 iOS 2.4.0

ARMSX2 iOS 2.4.0 is a big update focused on making the app feel better while you are actually playing.

The pause menu has been rebuilt, Per-Game Settings has been redesigned, more options can now be tuned per game, and a lot of rough edges around the library, audio, RetroAchievements, memory cards, icons, and compatibility have been cleaned up.

This update also brings over a large amount of platform and core work that helps improve performance, stability, and game compatibility across the app.

A big thank you to @isztldav and @jpolo1224  for the amount of platform work that helped make many of these features possible. A lot of this update builds on work that started across macOS and Android before being adapted and polished for iOS.

Thank you to Bagas for the new app icons.

New pause menu

The old in-game menu has been replaced with a new full-screen pause overlay.

It opens instantly, pauses gameplay while it is open, and uses a cleaner graphite layout with grouped actions. Resume is now pinned clearly in the footer, so getting back into the game feels more deliberate.

The new pause menu is split into clearer sections for quick actions, game-specific options, tools, reset, and exit. It also shows the active controller skin and layout, so it is easier to see what setup you are using without digging through settings.

The paused-game background now uses a stable dim instead of a blur effect. This keeps the menu readable and avoids the washed-out look that could happen over a paused game frame.

The pause menu also behaves better when returning from the background. If a game was running and you switch back to the app, the pause menu opens first instead of dropping you straight back into gameplay.

The Q Menu / pause button has also been cleaned up. It should stay visible, restore correctly if hidden, and no longer leave controller-only users stuck without a way back into the menu.

Rebuilt Per-Game Settings

Per-Game Settings has had a full redesign.

The old tab layout has been replaced with a cleaner category list:

 General
 Graphics
 Audio
 CPU & Speedhacks
 Virtual Pad
 Fixes & Compatibility
 Cheats & Patches

The panel now matches the new pause menu style, with a darker graphite look, a proper Save / Cancel footer, and protection against losing changes by accident.

If you try to close the panel with unsaved changes, the app now asks before discarding them. If there are no changes, Cancel simply becomes Close.

Opening Per-Game Settings should also feel faster now, since overrides are loaded in a cleaner pass instead of through lots of small reads.

There are many more per-game options now, including:

 FXAA
 Shade Boost
 brightness, contrast, saturation, and gamma
 TV / CRT shader
 CAS sharpening and sharpness
 max anisotropy
 screen offsets
 overscan
 anti-blur
 disable interlace offset
 integer scaling
 skip duplicate frames
 dithering
 hardware download mode
 CPU / GPU CLUT
 VSync queue size
 sync to host refresh
 texture replacement options
 fast-forward volume
 audio buffer size and latency
 IOP, VU0, and VU1 recompilers
 EE Cycle Skip
 widescreen patches
 no-interlacing patches
 per-game renderer selection
 Accurate Alpha Test
 Texture Inside RT
 manual game fixes such as OPH Flag, Skip MPEG, Instant DMA, VU Sync, GIF FIFO, Full VU0 Sync, and more

Visual settings can now apply while a game is running. Slider changes are handled more carefully too, so dragging a slider should not stall gameplay the way it could before.

Per-game Fast Boot has also been fixed so it applies correctly at boot without leaking the resolved value back into global settings.

Better landscape support

Landscape layouts have been cleaned up across iPhone and iPad.

The pause menu and Per-Game Settings now use floating rounded panels instead of awkward edge-to-edge layouts. Safe areas around the notch, Dynamic Island, and virtual pad are handled better.

Large iPhones like Pro Max and Plus models now use the correct phone landscape layout instead of accidentally being treated like iPads.

iPad keeps the larger layout, including a two-column pause menu and a rail/detail Per-Game Settings view in landscape.

Library improvements

The game library now supports animated backgrounds.

GIF, APNG, and animated WebP files can be used behind the game grid. Animations are decoded more carefully, capped for safety, pause in the background, and respect Reduce Motion by falling back to a static frame.

The library also now has a persisted metadata cache. Game title, serial, CRC, and region metadata can be reused across launches, so unchanged games do not need to be fully scanned every time.

Game cards have also been polished. They line up better, handle longer titles more cleanly, support Dynamic Type better, and show region flags.

Alternate app icons

2.4.0 adds alternate app icons under Appearance.

The included icons are:

 Default

LiveContainer installs also get an export fallback. If the container cannot change the Home Screen icon directly, you can export the icon and use it as a shortcut or container icon instead.

Audio changes

There is a new Left / Right Channel Swap option.

This is useful for flipped-speaker setups or reverse-landscape setups where the stereo channels feel backwards. It applies live without needing a restart.

The emulator volume slider now goes up to 150%. The default is unchanged, but values above 100% can amplify the output. As usual with amplification, it may distort depending on the game and device volume.

There is also an on-screen notifications toggle for transient in-game messages.

A mute-after-menu issue has been fixed as well. Audio should no longer stay muted after opening the menu during certain save-state or settings flows.

2.4.0 also includes an optional SPU2 NEON reverb path on iOS. This is an advanced INI-only option for now. There is no iOS UI toggle for it yet.

RetroAchievements

RetroAchievements now has sounds for unlocks, messages, and leaderboard submits.

Hardcore Mode is safer to disable now. The app asks for confirmation before turning it off, so a stray tap should not accidentally drop you out of Hardcore.

The old “softcore” wording has also been updated to “Casual.”

Memory-card improvements

Memory cards can now be deleted from settings, with confirmation.

If a deleted card was assigned to slot 1 or slot 2, that slot is cleared automatically. Slots also self-heal if a card was removed outside the app, such as through the Files app.

Cards currently loaded in slot 1 or 2 are now marked in the list, making it easier to see what is active.

Performance and compatibility

This update includes a large batch of arm64 recompiler work.

Several Emotion Engine paths that previously had to fall back to slower handling now have native arm64 coverage, including MADD-related paths, HI/LO handling, BC0/CPCOND0 behavior, DMA wait-loop handling, EI/ERET, COP0 Count/PERF handling, DI, traps, SYNC/CACHE, and SkipMPEGHack.

In practice, this should help performance and compatibility in some titles, especially games that are heavy on DMA, timing loops, or paths that previously hit fallback behavior.

The MTGS spin-wait window has also been reduced on Apple silicon, which should reduce wasted CPU time during frame handoff and help thermals and battery behavior.

Graphics and stability fixes

A number of shared-core fixes are included in this release.

Texture-replacement packs with an off-by-one mip count should no longer crash.

Shader and pipeline cache handling has been made safer, which should reduce the chance of broken cache data causing rendering issues after a crash or interrupted write.

Several texture-cache and framebuffer handling fixes have been brought in, which should help with corruption, stretched frames, or incorrect rendering in affected games.

The on-screen display scale is now capped so overlays stay readable on high-DPI screens.

DEV9 now has a DNS fallback on iOS, which helps hostname resolution for online and HDD features.

Game compatibility

The GameDB has been synced with upstream and includes targeted compatibility updates.

Notable fixes and tuning include:

 Jackie Chan Adventures clamp fixes
 Ace Combat 5 / Zero partial texture preloading
 Gran Turismo tuning
 Burnout 3 memory-card cross-save filters
 standalone ELF / homebrew per-game settings lookup fixes

This should be understood as an upstream GameDB sync plus targeted fixes, not as thousands of newly added games.

Other fixes and cleanup

iOS no longer shows some irrelevant startup warnings, such as warnings about controller bindings that do not make sense with the virtual pad, or renderer warnings that do not apply to the iOS setup.

The performance overlay now shows extra rendering status when relevant, and in-game navigation behaves better after surface resize or orientation changes.

There was also a cleanup pass through stale code paths, unused bridge methods, unused virtual-pad helpers, old localization strings, and other internal leftovers.

Final note

A huge thank you to the testing team.

This update had a lot of moving parts, and the amount of testing, retesting, feedback, and bug reports behind it made a real difference. A lot of the polish in 2.4.0 only happened because people spent real time using rough builds and pointing out what still needed work.

apps.subtitle: The newest features, built most days. Installs beside the stable app.
apps.localizedDescription:
The newest ARMSX2 features, built from the latest code most days. Less tested than a release, so expect the odd bug.

Most builds run fine. Now and then one carries a bug a release would have caught, or does not start. If you would rather play than test, install ARMSX2 iOS.

Nightly installs as its own app, next to the stable release rather than over it. Save states, memory cards and settings stay separate, so trying a nightly cannot disturb a working stable install. Nothing is shared between them either, so anything you save in one stays there.

Requirements
The same as the stable release: iPhone or iPad on iOS 17 or later, a JIT-capable setup, and your own PS2 BIOS and game files.
